body:
Implements the scope proposed in #576: a local, per-project "time spent" tracker.

**What it does**

- New `ProjectUsageTracker` (`sources/project/projectusagetracker.{h,cpp}`) accumulates how long a project has been the active tab. Uses `QElapsedTimer` and computes the total on demand in `secondsSpent()` — no polling/ticking timer needed.
- Hosted on `ProjectPropertiesHandler`, per that class's own doc comment: *"All new properties should be managed by this class."*
- Persisted as a new `<usage time_spent="N" enabled="true|false"/>` element, a sibling of `<properties>` in the project XML — written/read by new `QETProject::writeUsageXml()`/`readUsageXml()`. It's picked up by the existing autosave path automatically, since `writeBackup()` already serializes the full project via `toXml()`.
- `QETDiagramEditor::subWindowActivated()` now pauses every open project's tracker except whichever one's tab just became current, so tracked time stays isolated per project when several are open.
- Surfaced in the existing Project Properties "Général" page: a "Temps passé sur ce projet" display, a "Réinitialiser" button, and an opt-out checkbox — explicitly labelled as local-only, never transmitted anywhere.

**Why this shape** (from the discussion)

- Kept deliberately separate from `m_project_properties` (the `DiagramContext` backing the user-editable Custom-variables tab) so an automatic counter can't be accidentally edited/deleted alongside a user's own variables.
- No telemetry, no network code anywhere in this — the value lives only in the project's own file.

**Testing**

Beyond compiling clean (`-fsyntax-only` on every touched file, then a full CMake build with only the two pre-existing unrelated deprecation warnings already in `master`), I ran this end-to-end in a real session:

- Created a project, let it accumulate time, saved, and confirmed the actual XML: `<usage enabled="true" time_spent="179"/>`.
- Closed and reopened the file — the value round-tripped and timing resumed immediately on reopen.
- Reset button verified to zero the display instantly.
- **Key correctness check**: opened a second project. Over the same real-time interval, the first (now inactive) project's `time_spent` stayed frozen at exactly `100` while the second (active) project accumulated `95` — confirming the pause/resume gating correctly isolates tracked time per project with no bleed-through.

*Developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).*

long a project has been the active tab, using QElapsedTimer so the
value is computed on demand rather than via polling. It's hosted on
ProjectPropertiesHandler per that class's own stated design intent
("all new properties should be managed by this class").

The accumulated time is persisted as a new <usage time_spent="N"
enabled="true|false"/> element, a sibling of <properties> in the
project XML, written/read by new QETProject::writeUsageXml()/
readUsageXml(). It rides along on the existing autosave path for
free, since writeBackup() already serializes the full project via
toXml().

QETDiagramEditor::subWindowActivated() now pauses every open
project's tracker except the one whose tab just became current, so
switching between several open projects keeps each project's tracked
time isolated.

Surfaced in the existing Project Properties "Général" page: a
"Temps passé sur ce projet" display, a "Réinitialiser" button, and
an opt-out checkbox ("uniquement enregistré localement dans ce

Verified beyond compiling: full CMake build, then an actual runtime
session confirming the saved XML's time_spent value, that closing
and reopening the project round-trips and resumes timing, that the
reset button works, and - the key correctness check - that with two
projects open, the inactive one's time_spent stays frozen while the
active one accumulates real elapsed time, over the same interval.

See discussion #576.
